verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown into the Pacific Ocean... 8:07 p.m. ET/5:07 p.m. PT... near San Diego, California.' R2: 'splashdown... off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).' R4: 'splash down... off the coast of San Diego... at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET on Friday, April 10, 2026.' R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California... 8:07 p.m. ET'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm exact location, date, time, and safe splashdown.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II was on a 10-day mission'. R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'. R4: '10-day mission'. R5: '10-day mission'. R6: '10-day journey'.
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state the mission duration as 10 days, concluding with splashdown.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams immediately attended to the four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN!... The recovery team is on site and headed to the capsule... 8:12 p.m.... approaching the spacecraft'. R5: 'Within two hours after splashdown, recovery teams will retrieve the crew'. R6: 'astronauts were taken to the recovery ship... getting pulled out of the Orion capsule'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm prompt recovery team action post-splashdown for the four crew members.

verifications.claim: The crew module separated from the service module at 7:33 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crew module separation at 7:33 p.m. ET'. R2: '7:33 p.m. Orion’s crew and service module have separated'. R5: '7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate from the service module'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and event directly stated in multiple sources on April 10 context.

verifications.claim: The capsule hit the upper atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet above'. R5: '7:53 p.m.: The spacecraft makes first contact with the upper atmosphere'.
verifications.reasoning: Precise time and atmospheric entry directly matched in sources.

verifications.claim: The capsule hit the upper atmosphere causing a 6-minute communication blackout.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '7:53 p.m... planned communications blackout expected to last about six minutes as plasma built around the crew capsule'. R3: 'lose communication for about six minutes as the Orion capsule... is enveloped in a fireball'. R5: '7:53 p.m... planned 6-minute communications blackout as plasma builds around the capsule'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources link upper atmosphere entry directly to ~6-minute blackout.

verifications.claim: The capsule reached the water at 8:07 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... 8:07 p.m. ET'. R2: '8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN!... parachute-assisted splashdown'. R4: 'splash down... 8:07 p.m. ET on Friday, April 10, 2026'. R5: '8:07 p.m.: ... Orion will splash down'. R6: 'splashed down... at 8:07 p.m. ET'.
verifications.reasoning: Splashdown time (reaching water) exactly matches across sources.

verifications.claim: The crew was recovered by the U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'transported... to the USS John P. Murtha, which is a U.S. Navy transport dock ship'. R2: 'USS John P. Murtha... recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha'. R3: 'U.S.S. John P. Murtha... recovery ship'. R6: 'USS John P. Murtha recovery vessel... All four astronauts are on board the recovery ship'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm recovery by the named U.S. Navy ship.
